notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: Frustrated with this distinctly Japanese style, she became interested in the European and American avant-garde, staging several solo exhibitions of her paintings in Matsumoto and Tokyo in the 1950s.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
src.q: She went on to study Nihonga painting at the Kyoto Municipal School of Arts and Crafts in 1948.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
src.q: In 1957, she moved to Seattle, where she had an exhibition of paintings at the Zoe Dusanne Gallery.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: In 1959, Kusama had her first solo exhibition in New York at the Brata Gallery, an artist's co-op.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: Her first exhibition that earned great success was in 1959 at the Brata Gallery and then she went on to pioneering body art performances and "happenings".

src.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
src.q: She moved to New York City in 1958 and was a part of the New York avant-garde scene throughout the 1960s, especially in the pop-art movement.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: Perhaps one of Kusama's most notorious works, various versions of Narcissus Garden have been presented worldwide venues including Le Consortium, Dijon, 2000; Kunstverein Braunschweig, 2003; as part of the Whitney Biennial at Central Park, New York in 2004; and at the Jardin de Tuileries in Paris, 2010.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: She harkened back to earlier work by returning to drawing and painting; her work remained innovative and multi-disciplinary, and a 2012 exhibition displayed multiple acrylic-on-canvas works.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: In 2017, a 50-year retrospective of her work opened at the Hirshhorn Museum in Washington, D.C..

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: On 25 February 2017, Kusama's All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins exhibit, one of the six components to her Infinity Mirror rooms at the Hirshhorn Museum, was temporarily closed for three days following damage to one of the exhibit's glowing pumpkin sculptures.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: In 2017, a fifty-year retrospective of Kusama's work opened at the Hirshhorn Museum in Washington, DC.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
src.q: 30 June 2017 – 10 September 2017: Yayoi Kusama: Infinity Mirrors, exhibition traveled to Seattle Art Museum

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: On 9 November 2019, Kusama's Everyday I Pray For Love exhibition was shown at David Zwirner Gallery until 14 December.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: In January 2020, the Hirshhorn announced it would debut new Kusama acquisitions, including two Infinity Mirror Rooms, at a forthcoming exhibition called One with Eternity: Yayoi Kusama in the Hirshhorn Collection.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: According to Hanna Schouwink of David Zwirner Gallery speaking in 2018, Kusama is "officially the world's most successful living artist".

src.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
src.q: 7 July 2018 – 30 September 2018: Yayoi Kusama: Infinity Mirrors, exhibition traveled to Cleveland Museum of Art, Cleveland, Ohio

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: The exhibition, which showed until May 2023, was the largest retrospective of her art in Asia, not including her home country.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: In 2024, Kusama unveiled a new Infinity Mirror Room titled Infinity Mirrored Room – Beauty Described by a Spherical Heart as part of her solo exhibition Every Day I Pray for Love at the Victoria Miro Gallery in London.

src.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
src.q: 15 November 2021 – 23 April 2022: Yayoi Kusama: A Retrospective, exhibition traveled to Tel Aviv Museum of Art

notes.name: Wikipedia · Yayoi Kusama
notes.q: In 2025–2026, a major European retrospective of Yayoi Kusama traces seven decades of her career through paintings, sculptures and immersive installations, travelling from the Fondation Beyeler in Switzerland to Museum Ludwig in Cologne and the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.
